title: Bahrain | CBB Corporate Governance, Fit and Proper and Board Training (Modules HC and FP)
tagline: Bahrain's board rules in practice: Module HC duties, committees and conduct, director induction, Module FP approvals and CPD.
sectors: Conventional banks licensed by the Central Bank of Bahrain
Boards of directors and board committees
Compliance, risk management and internal audit
Human resources and learning teams in banks
description:
A country-specific quest for **conventional banks licensed by the Central Bank of Bahrain (CBB)** under Volume 1 of the CBB Rulebook. It is built on the **Central Bank of Bahrain and Financial Institutions Law (Law No. 64 of 2006)**, in particular Articles 38 and 65, the CBB's **High-Level Controls Module (Module HC)** for bank licensees and the **Fit and Proper Requirements Module (Module FP)** in the Common Volume.

**Versions used:** Module HC paragraphs come from the revised text the CBB published for consultation in July 2022; the CBB reports that it issued the revised module in March 2023, with new requirements effective 1 October 2023. Module FP paragraphs, including the 15-hour CPD minimum, come from the CBB-hosted consultation text of October 2024; the final module was issued in March 2025 (prior approvals from 1 April 2025, the rest from 1 October 2025). The in-force Rulebook site blocks automated access, so check the current wording there.

It is for directors, senior managers, company secretaries and compliance, risk, audit and HR staff who must know how the CBB expects boards to govern, train and stay fit and proper. It builds knowledge and does not replace your bank's own policies, charters and procedures.
audience: Board members and board committee members of CBB-licensed conventional banks
Chief executives and heads of senior management functions covered by Module FP
Company secretaries and corporate governance officers who run board processes
Compliance, risk management and internal audit staff with HC training and reporting duties
HR and learning teams who build induction, training plans and CPD records
outcomes: Explain how the CBB Law and Module HC set the board's responsibilities, composition, meetings and attendance rules
Apply Module HC's committee, code of conduct, conflict of interest and whistleblowing requirements
Design a director induction and ongoing training approach that meets HC-2.3 and Module FP
Apply Module FP's fit and proper criteria, approval, notification and record rules to appointments
Describe the training duties for senior management, risk, compliance and internal audit staff and the evidence the CBB expects

quest.name: The Arad Bay Boardroom
quest.premise: You have joined the corporate governance office of Arad Bay Bank, a fictional conventional retail bank licensed by the CBB with its head office in Seef, Manama. A new independent director arrives next month, Module FP is fully in force and the CBB's prudential meeting is six weeks away. With compliance head Huda Al Arrayedh, chair Ebrahim Naser, audit head Priya Raghunathan, new director Marcus Lindqvist and CEO Salman Al Haddad, build the bank's governance and training file stage by stage, then face the final boss: the board's review.

badge.name: Bahrain Board Steward
badge.description: Awarded to bank staff who can apply the CBB's Module HC and Module FP: govern well, train the board and keep every key person fit and proper.

cast.name: Huda Al Arrayedh
cast.role: Head of Compliance and Governance Officer, your mentor

sessions.title: Bahrain's Governance Rulebook: the CBB Law, Module HC and the Board's Mandate
sessions.summary: Where the CBB's governance powers come from, how Module HC applies to conventional bank licensees, what the board must do, and the composition, independence and attendance rules the CBB checks every year.
objectives: Explain where the CBB's governance powers come from (CBB Law Articles 38 and 65) and how Module HC applies to conventional banks
Describe the board's core responsibilities and its oversight of senior management under HC-1.1 and HC-1.3
Apply Module HC's board composition, independence, chairperson and attendance rules
Distinguish Rules that must be followed from Guidance that is subject to comply or explain

cards.title: Six weeks to the prudential meeting
cards.setting: Arad Bay Bank head office, Seef. Monday, 8:30 am.

lines.text: Welcome aboard. Our prudential meeting with the CBB is in six weeks, and board effectiveness is on the agenda.
And a new independent director, Marcus Lindqvist, joins next month. His induction has to be ready on day one.
Is an induction a nice extra, or does the CBB actually require it?
Module HC requires it. The board must budget for induction every year and give each new director a tailored programme with ongoing training.
As chair, I want one file that shows the CBB how this board works: duties, committees, conduct, fit and proper and training.
That's our quest: five stages, then we present the file to the board. Stage one: what the Rulebook expects from a board.

cards.title: Where the board's duties come from

scenes.heading: The CBB Law
scenes.narration: Law No. 64 of 2006 sets out the Central Bank of Bahrain's powers. Article 38 lets the Governor issue binding directives, and Article 65 deals with approval of, and standards for, the people who run a licensee.

scenes.heading: The Rulebook
scenes.narration: The CBB issues its directives as the CBB Rulebook. Volume 1 covers conventional banks, and Module HC, High-Level Controls, holds the corporate governance rules.

scenes.heading: Rules and Guidance
scenes.narration: Paragraphs classed as Rules must be followed. Guidance works on comply or explain: a bank that departs from it explains why in its annual report, or the CBB may treat it as a breach of a Rule.

scenes.heading: Fit and proper
scenes.narration: Since 2025, a separate Module FP in the Common Volume sets fit and proper rules for every licensee, including training for directors and senior managers.

scenes.heading: Proportionality
scenes.narration: Module HC is applied in line with a bank's size, complexity and risk profile. For branches of foreign banks, the board means the head office or regional office.

cards.title: How today's governance rules arrived
cards.caption: Dates from the CBB Law, the CBB's 2023 Annual Report and CBB press releases. Always check the in-force Rulebook text.

items.label: CBB Law enacted
items.detail: Law No. 64 of 2006 sets the CBB's powers, including Article 65 on a licensee's board and executives.

items.label: Revised HC consulted on
items.detail: The CBB publishes a restructured High-Level Controls Module for bank licensees for consultation.

items.label: Revised HC issued
items.detail: Issued for bank licensees, with a gap analysis and action plan due to the CBB by 31 May 2023.

items.label: New HC rules apply
items.detail: The newly added Module HC requirements take effect for banks.

items.label: FP consultation
items.detail: A proposed Fit and Proper Module is published to replace older fit and proper and competency rules.

items.label: Module FP issued
items.detail: The final Module FP is issued in the Common Volume for all licensees.

items.label: Module FP in force
items.detail: Prior-approval rules from 1 April 2025; the remaining requirements from 1 October 2025.

cards.question: A Guidance paragraph in Module HC does not suit Arad Bay Bank's structure. What does the comply-or-explain principle allow?
options: The bank may depart from it if it explains the non-compliance in its annual report
The bank may ignore it, because only Rules have legal effect
The bank must ask the CBB for a written waiver before each board meeting
The bank may apply it at head office only and skip it elsewhere
cards.explanation: Guidance can be departed from, but the bank must explain why in its annual report. If it gives no explanation, or an unsatisfactory one, the CBB can treat the gap as non-compliance with a Rule, so ignoring Guidance silently is not an option.

cards.title: What the board must do (HC-1.1)
cards.body:
Under Module HC the board of a conventional bank must, among other things:

- **Set the tone at the top** and oversee how management builds a sound corporate and risk culture.
- **Prevent domination:** no person or group may hold unfettered decision power.
- **Approve strategy, plans and budget** and monitor them. Bahraini banks send their strategy and major changes to the CBB for review.
- **Approve the governance and risk frameworks and all policies**, reviewing them when the business, the rules or the controls change.
- **Set the risk appetite** with senior management and the chief risk officer.
- **Ensure** that controls work, the bank complies with the CBB Law and the Rulebook, and risk, compliance and internal audit are independent and resourced.
- **Approve the selection** of the CEO, CFO and heads of risk, compliance and internal audit, and oversee their performance.

The board can delegate functions to its committees, but **never its responsibilities**.

cards.title: Board, committee or management?
cards.prompt: Under Module HC, who carries each duty at Arad Bay Bank?

items.text: Approve the annual financial statements
Approve the selection of the CEO and the heads of control functions
Set the risk appetite together with management and the CRO
Recommend appointing or dismissing the head of internal audit
Assess once a year how well compliance risk is managed
Recommend candidates for the board and for CEO
Run daily business within the board-approved risk appetite
Tell the board promptly about frauds, limit breaches and whistleblowing issues

cards.title: Board composition at a glance (Bahraini bank)
cards.caption: From the CBB-hosted text of the revised Module HC. Items marked Guidance are comply or explain.

items.label: Independence
items.right: A sufficient number; at least one third of the board where the bank has a controller

items.label: Non-executives
items.right: Guidance: at least half the board, with at least three independent directors

items.label: Chair
items.right: Not an executive and not the CEO; Guidance says the chair should be independent

items.label: Meetings
items.right: At least four a year, with half of them held in Bahrain

items.label: Attendance
items.right: At least 75% of board meetings a year; proxies prohibited

items.label: Long service
items.right: Lost after three consecutive terms on the board

lines.text: One director attended only five of eight board meetings last year. He says he was travelling and sent a colleague as his proxy.
Two problems. Proxies for board meetings are prohibited, and with eight meetings the 75% minimum means six.
So what do we have to do?
Notify the CBB immediately, with his attendance and the reasons. The CBB then decides whether enforcement under Article 65 of the CBB Law is appropriate.
And our board framework should expect a director who isn't taking part to step down.

cards.title: Handling the missed meetings
cards.situation: It is January. The company secretary confirms that a non-executive director attended five of eight board meetings last financial year and twice sent a colleague as his proxy. He stands for re-election at the general meeting in March. The chair asks you what the bank should do.

choices.text: Notify the CBB now with his attendance and reasons, keep absences minuted, report his attendance at the AGM and ask the nomination committee to review his position
choices.outcome: Best answer. Module HC requires immediate notice to the CBB, absences noted in minutes and attendance reported when a director stands for re-election. The CBB decides whether Article 65 action is needed, and the board deals with non-participation through its own framework.

choices.text: Send the director a reminder of the 75% rule and watch his attendance more closely next year
choices.outcome: A reminder helps, but it skips the duty to notify the CBB immediately and to disclose his attendance to shareholders before re-election.

choices.text: Count the two proxy attendances as present, which brings him to seven of eight
choices.outcome: Proxies are prohibited, so counting them would misstate attendance to the CBB and to shareholders. That turns one breach into a second, more serious one.

choices.text: Wait until after the March AGM so the re-election is not disrupted, then inform the CBB
choices.outcome: The notice must be immediate, and attendance must be reported to shareholders when the director stands for re-election. Delaying hides material facts from both.

items.label: Meet regularly
items.detail: The board meets senior management regularly, not only at formal sessions.

items.label: Assess yearly
items.detail: Senior management gets an annual, documented performance assessment.

items.label: Challenge
items.detail: Directors question and critically review what management tells them.

items.label: Check compliance
items.detail: Management acts within law, strategy, policies and the risk appetite.

items.label: Plan succession
items.detail: Succession plans for approved persons in senior management, reviewed when they change.

cards.title: Directors' duties in plain words
cards.prompt: Match each Module HC duty of an individual director to what it means in practice.

pairs.right: Act with care, candour and loyalty to the bank under local law
Act for the bank as a whole, not only for the shareholder who nominated you
Make sure papers arrive in good time and study them carefully
Understand board duties under the Rulebook, the Commercial Companies Law and other laws
Recognise a specific responsibility to minority shareholders

cards.question: Arad Bay Bank has a controlling shareholder and nine directors. What is the minimum independence requirement in Module HC?
options: At least half the board must be independent, so five directors
At least one third of the board must be independent, so three directors
Two independent directors, whatever the size of the board
Only the chairperson has to be independent
cards.explanation: Where a Bahraini bank has a controller, at least one third of the board must be independent: three of nine. The half figure in Module HC is Guidance on non-executive directors, not a rule on independent directors.

cards.title: Real case: the CBB's revised HC rollout (2023)
cards.body:
In its **2023 Annual Report**, the CBB describes how it introduced the revised High-Level Controls Module for banks:

- In **March 2023** it issued the revised Module HC for bank licensees, with related changes to its reporting, operational risk and public disclosure modules.
- The newly added requirements took effect on **1 October 2023**.
- Every bank had to assess what needed to change in its policies, procedures, processes and systems and send the CBB a **gap analysis and an implementation action plan by 31 May 2023**.
- The CBB later split the module into Part One for Bahraini banks and Part Two for branches of foreign banks.

**Lesson for Arad Bay:** new governance rules arrive with a transition window. The board should own the gap analysis and track the action plan to closure, not leave it to compliance alone.

Source: CBB Annual Report 2023, cbb.gov.bh.

cards.title: Real case: what CBB supervisors check (2023-2024)
cards.body:
The CBB's annual reports describe how its banking supervisors monitor boards:

- **2023:** supervisors reviewed banks' annual corporate governance reports, directors' attendance and participation, board committee structures and the appointment of independent directors. They also assessed compliance with the enhanced Module HC, including its rules on ethical conduct and whistleblowing.
- **2024:** the reviews again covered attendance, the role directors play in meetings, committee structures, independent directors and conflicts of interest, and the CBB also looked at banks' organisation structures and succession plans.
- Each year the CBB holds **prudential meetings** with banks on performance, strategy and supervisory issues.

**Lesson:** the governance file is evidence. Minutes, attendance records, evaluations and succession plans are what supervisors read.

Sources: CBB Annual Reports 2023 and 2024, cbb.gov.bh.

cards.title: Stage 1 take-aways
items: Module HC is a CBB directive under Article 38 of the CBB Law; Rules must be followed and Guidance is comply or explain.
The board sets culture, strategy, risk appetite and policies, and can delegate functions but never responsibility.
A Bahraini bank with a controller needs at least one third independent directors; the chair must not be an executive or the CEO.
At least four board meetings a year, half in Bahrain; each director attends 75% or more, with no proxies.
Falling below 75% attendance must be notified to the CBB immediately, which may consider Article 65 action.

cards.prompt: Think of a board or senior committee you have seen at work. Where would a CBB supervisor find evidence that it challenges management, and where would they find gaps?

quiz.question: Under which article of the CBB Law does the Governor issue the binding directives that make up Module HC?
options: Article 65
Article 129
Article 132
Article 38
quiz.explanation: Module HC states it is a CBB directive issued under Article 38, which lets the Governor issue binding directives. Article 65 is about approval of and standards for a licensee's officials, which Module FP relies on, not the source of Module HC.

quiz.question: Arad Bay Bank holds eight board meetings this year. Under Module HC, how many must each director attend at least?
options: Five meetings
Seven meetings
Six meetings
Four meetings
quiz.explanation: Each director must attend at least 75% of board meetings; Module HC's table shows six of eight. Five of eight is only 62.5%, below the minimum.

quiz.question: A director cannot attend a board meeting and wants a colleague to attend and vote for him. What does Module HC say?
options: Attendance and voting proxies are prohibited
Proxies are allowed if the chair agrees
Proxies are allowed for up to two meetings in a financial year
Proxies are allowed for non-executives only
quiz.explanation: HC-3.1.8 prohibits voting and attendance proxies for board meetings. There is no exception for the chair's consent or for non-executive directors.

quiz.question: Which statement about the chairperson of a Bahraini bank's board matches Module HC?
options: The chair may also be the CEO if shareholders approve it at the AGM
The chair must not be an executive director or the CEO
The chair must also chair the audit committee
The chair is appointed directly by the CBB
quiz.explanation: HC-3.2.1 says the chair must not be an executive director and must not be the same person as the CEO. The audit committee chair must not be the board chair unless independent, and the CBB does not appoint chairs.

quiz.question: Arad Bay's board delegated the review of the risk policy to the risk committee. A large loss follows. Who remains responsible for the risk policy?
options: The risk committee alone, since it received the delegated review task
The chief risk officer, who drafted the policy
The board, which may delegate functions but not responsibility
Management, as the delegation moved the duty to them
quiz.explanation: HC-1.1.2 lets the board delegate functions to committees but not its responsibilities. The risk committee advises and oversees, but the board stays accountable for the policies it approves.

quiz.question: Under HC-1.1, what must a Bahraini bank's board submit to the CBB for review?
options: Every board paper before each meeting
Its proposed strategy and any major changes to it
Each director's personal financial statements
Monthly branch staffing rotas
quiz.explanation: HC-1.1.1(c) requires Bahraini bank licensees to submit their proposed strategy and major proposed changes to it to the CBB. The other items are not CBB submissions under Module HC.

quiz.question: An independent director of Arad Bay is proposed for reappointment after three consecutive terms. How must the bank classify him?
options: No longer independent if he is reappointed
Still independent if he has no family ties
Independent for one more term with CBB notice
Independent if shareholders vote to confirm it
quiz.explanation: HC-2.3.2 says a director who has served three consecutive terms loses independent status and must not be classed as independent if reappointed. Family ties, CBB notice or a shareholder vote do not restore it.

quiz.question: What does HC-1.3 require the board to do when overseeing senior management?
options: Approve every credit decision that senior managers take during the year
Attend all management committee meetings
Set each manager's daily objectives
Assess their performance every year and document it
quiz.explanation: HC-1.3.1(b) requires annual, documented performance assessments of senior management. The board oversees and challenges; it does not take over management decisions or meetings.

quiz.question: Arad Bay does not follow a Guidance paragraph of Module HC and its annual report says nothing about it. How may the CBB treat this?
options: As acceptable, because Guidance paragraphs can never be enforced by the CBB
As non-compliance with a Rule, since no explanation was given
As a matter for shareholders to raise at the AGM
As a breach only if a customer complains
quiz.explanation: Under comply or explain, non-compliance with Guidance must be explained in the annual report. Without a satisfactory explanation the CBB treats it as non-compliance with a Rule, so silence is not safe.

quiz.question: A director's attendance falls below 75% of board meetings for the year. What must Arad Bay do under Module HC?
options: Mention it in next year's annual report and corporate governance report
Wait for the CBB to raise it at inspection
Fine the director under the board charter
Notify the CBB immediately with his attendance and the reasons
quiz.explanation: HC-3.1.10 requires immediate notice to the CBB naming the director, his attendance and the reasons. The CBB then considers action under Article 65 of the CBB Law; delay or internal fines do not meet the duty.

sessions.title: Committees, Culture and Conduct: Codes, Conflicts and Whistleblowing
sessions.summary: The four committees every Bahraini bank board needs, the board's duties on values and the code of conduct, the conflict of interest policy for approved persons, and how the whistleblowing policy protects people who speak up.
objectives: Describe the mandatory board committees of a Bahraini bank and their key composition rules
Explain the board's duties on corporate values and the code of conduct under HC-1.2.1
Apply the conflict of interest policy requirements to approved persons
Explain how the whistleblowing policy protects staff and how material concerns can reach the CBB

cards.title: The supplier contract
cards.setting: Arad Bay Bank, board papers review. Tuesday morning.

lines.text: The facilities contract renewal is on the board agenda. One bidder is a company in which a director's brother is a major shareholder.
Under our conflict of interest policy that is a personal interest: family includes brothers and sisters. He must disclose and abstain.
I'm new here. What if the board still wants to award the contract to that company?
Then a transaction where an approved person has a material conflict needs formal, unanimous approval by the entire board, on arm's length terms.
There's more. Internal audit received an anonymous note through the whistleblowing channel saying the bid scores were changed.
Then we protect whoever raised it and decide properly who investigates. Huda, take us through the rules.

scenes.heading: Values
scenes.narration: The board sets corporate values that expect business to be done legally, professionally and ethically, and it oversees how directors, managers and staff live up to them.

scenes.heading: Code of conduct
scenes.narration: The board approves a code of conduct that spells out acceptable and unacceptable practices for everyone, from directors to new joiners.

scenes.heading: Communicate
scenes.narration: Values, professional standards and the code are communicated across the whole bank, and everyone knows that misconduct leads to disciplinary action.

scenes.heading: Risk culture
scenes.narration: The board promotes risk awareness and makes clear that every employee helps keep the bank inside its risk appetite and limits.

scenes.heading: Speak up
scenes.narration: Staff can raise concerns confidentially and without reprisal through a board-approved whistleblowing policy, which includes escalating material concerns to the CBB.

cards.title: From concern to accountability (HC-1.2.2 and HC-1.2.3)

items.label: Raise
items.detail: A member of staff raises a legitimate concern confidentially through the whistleblowing channel.

items.label: Protect
items.detail: The board makes sure the person is shielded from reprisal and detrimental treatment.

items.label: Assign
items.detail: The board approves how, and by whom, material concerns are investigated.

items.label: Investigate
items.detail: An objective body, internal or external, tests whether the allegation is valid.

items.label: Act
items.detail: Whoever is responsible for misconduct is held accountable and disciplined.

items.label: Escalate
items.detail: Material concerns can be escalated to the CBB under the policy.

cards.question: Which statement about Arad Bay's code of conduct matches Module HC?
options: Human resources approves it, and only senior staff need to follow it
It binds employees but not members of the board
The board approves it and makes sure it is communicated across the bank
It is Guidance, so the bank may explain it away in the annual report
cards.explanation: HC-1.2.1 makes the board approve a code of conduct covering directors, senior management and all staff, and ensure it is communicated throughout the bank. It is a board duty, not an HR one, and it applies to the board itself.

cards.title: The conflict of interest policy (HC-1.2.4)
cards.body:
The board must adopt a conflict of interest policy for all approved persons. It covers:

- **Duties:** avoid conflicts where possible, disclose promptly, abstain where conflicted, never use the bank's property, assets, information or opportunities for personal gain, and never compete with the bank.
- **Personal interest:** includes close family (spouse, parents, children, brothers and sisters) and companies the person directs or controls.
- **Material conflicts:** entering such a transaction needs **formal, unanimous approval by the whole board**.
- **Related parties:** dealings on an arm's length basis, and controls on hiring relatives of approved persons.
- **Annual written declarations** of other interests, such as holdings above 5% of a company's voting capital.
- **Reporting** observed material conflict cases to the CBB.

Separately, the CEO tells the board each year which staff in controlled functions are relatives of approved persons.

cards.title: Does the policy ask for it?
cards.prompt: Sort each item: is it something Module HC requires in the conflict of interest policy, or does it go against the module?

items.text: Annual written declaration of other business interests
Arm's length terms for related party transactions
Restrictions or a transparent process for hiring relatives
Reporting observed material conflict cases to the CBB
Review before an approved person joins another board
A simple majority vote, including the conflicted director
No disclosure needed for deals with a sibling's company
Approved persons may compete with the bank once they disclose it

cards.title: The four committees every Bahraini bank board needs
cards.caption: HC-3.3.1 requires audit, risk, remuneration and nomination committees. A corporate governance committee is Guidance.

items.label: Audit
items.left: 3+ directors, majority independent; independent chair; no CEO or senior managers
items.right: Financial reporting, internal and external audit, compliance reports, code of conduct oversight

items.label: Risk
items.left: 3+ directors, majority independent, with risk experience; independent chair; no management
items.right: Risk strategy and appetite, CRO appointment, risk reporting and culture

items.label: Remuneration
items.left: 3+ directors, independent of any risk-taking function
items.right: Pay policy and packages for approved persons and material risk-takers

items.label: Nomination
items.left: 3 independent directors, or 3 non-executives with an independent majority and chair
items.right: Board and senior hires, succession plans, time commitment, effectiveness

cards.title: The anonymous note
cards.setting: Internal audit office, the next morning.

lines.text: The note says a procurement manager changed the scores after a call from 'upstairs'. The writer is afraid of being identified.
Upstairs? I want to know who sent this.
Salman, we must not hunt for the whistleblower. The board has to protect people who raise concerns from any reprisal.
And because it may involve senior management, the board should decide who investigates. Perhaps the audit committee with an outside firm.
Agreed. I'll take it to the audit committee chair today.

cards.title: Who investigates?
cards.situation: The whistleblowing report alleges that a senior manager influenced a supplier evaluation. The CEO offers to run the investigation himself 'to keep it quick and quiet'. Staff in procurement are already guessing who wrote the note. What should the board do?

choices.text: Have the audit committee commission an objective investigation independent of the managers involved, protect the reporter's confidentiality and discipline anyone found responsible
choices.outcome: Best answer. The board must decide how and by whom material concerns are investigated, protect the reporter and hold those responsible to account. An investigation independent of the people involved is what Module HC expects.

choices.text: Report the matter to the CBB straight away and take no internal action until the CBB replies
choices.outcome: Escalating material concerns to the CBB can be right, but the board still has to oversee an internal investigation and protect the reporter. Waiting passively leaves the issue unmanaged.

choices.text: Let the CEO investigate, since senior management must address the issues raised
choices.outcome: Senior management does address legitimate issues, but here the allegation points 'upstairs'. Letting a possibly conflicted executive run the inquiry undermines its objectivity.

choices.text: Ask procurement staff to identify the writer so the facts can be checked with them
choices.outcome: Hunting for the reporter breaks the confidentiality the policy promises and is exactly the kind of detrimental treatment the board must prevent.

cards.front: How often must the audit committee meet?
cards.back: At least four times a year, at least twice with the external auditor, and once a year without the CEO and executives but with compliance, internal audit and risk present.

cards.front: Who recommends hiring or dismissing the heads of internal audit and compliance?
cards.back: The audit committee. The bank must also discuss the reasons for a dismissal with the CBB.

cards.front: Who recommends the CRO's appointment or removal?
cards.back: The risk committee, which also discusses the reasons for removal with the CBB.

cards.front: How often is internal audit and compliance quality reviewed externally?
cards.back: Every five years, by a third-party consultant other than the external auditor, commissioned by the audit committee.
Only if no conflict arises between their duties, and with the CBB's prior approval.

cards.front: Who verifies governance compliance day to day?
cards.back: A corporate governance officer drawn from senior management; the compliance officer may take on the role.

cards.question: The audit committee chair of a Bahraini bank also wants to chair the risk committee. What does Module HC say?
options: It is allowed if the CBB is notified in advance
It is allowed as long as the chair is independent
It is allowed only for boards with fewer than seven directors
It is not allowed: the audit committee chair must not chair another committee
cards.explanation: HC-3.4.2 requires the audit committee chair to be independent and not to chair any other board committee. Independence alone does not cure the double chair, and there is no notification route around it.

cards.title: Real case: conflicts and whistleblowing under inspection (2024)
cards.body:
The CBB's **2024 Annual Report** explains how its Inspection Directorate examines banks' consumer protection practices. The framework covers strategy, governance and culture, product design, fair treatment of customers, disclosure and data privacy.

During 2024 the Directorate put **extensive focus** on:

- conflicts of interest and related party transactions;
- succession planning;
- whistleblowing frameworks; and
- customer centricity across the whole product life cycle.

**Lesson for Arad Bay:** conflict registers, related-party approvals and whistleblowing logs are reviewed on site. A policy that exists on paper but has an empty log, missing declarations or unrecorded board approvals is a finding waiting to happen.

Source: CBB Annual Report 2024, cbb.gov.bh.

cards.title: Real case: the CBB's compliance culture meetings (2023)
cards.body:
In its **2023 Annual Report**, the CBB records that its banking supervisors held meetings with banks on **customer centricity and compliance culture**. The meetings stressed that:

- senior management must promote a customer-centric culture and improve the quality of service;
- senior management is accountable for customer service failings;
- customer complaints should be resolved quickly; and
- banks should work on strengthening their compliance culture and ethical conduct.

**Lesson:** for the CBB, culture is not a slogan. It expects the board to set values, management to live them and the evidence (complaints data, conduct cases, training) to show it.

Source: CBB Annual Report 2023, cbb.gov.bh.

cards.title: Stage 2 take-aways
items: Every Bahraini bank board needs audit, risk, remuneration and nomination committees with written charters.
The CEO and senior managers may not sit on the audit or risk committee, and their chairs must be independent.
The board approves the code of conduct and makes sure it, the values and the consequences of misconduct are known by all.
Approved persons disclose and abstain; a material conflict transaction needs unanimous approval of the whole board.
Whistleblowers are protected from reprisal; the board decides who investigates, and material concerns can go to the CBB.

cards.prompt: If you had a serious concern at work today, would you know which channel to use and trust that you would be protected? What would make that channel more credible?

quiz.question: A director's brother owns 30% of a company bidding for an Arad Bay contract. Under the conflict of interest policy, what must the director do?
options: Vote on it as normal, as long as he declares the family link afterwards
Disclose it promptly and abstain from the discussion and vote
Nothing, because siblings fall outside the policy
Resign from the board before the vote is held
quiz.explanation: Module HC treats a brother's material interest as a personal interest of the approved person. He must disclose promptly and abstain. Siblings are expressly included, and resignation is not required.

quiz.question: The board still wants to award the contract to that company. What approval does Module HC require?
options: A simple majority of the directors present, excluding the conflicted one
Joint approval of the CEO and the CFO
Formal, unanimous approval of the entire board
Approval by the audit committee alone
quiz.explanation: HC-1.2.4 requires any decision to enter a transaction in which an approved person appears to have a material conflict to be formally and unanimously approved by the whole board. A majority or committee approval is not enough.

quiz.question: How often must approved persons declare their other business interests in writing under HC-1.2.4?
options: Every three years
Only on appointment
Only when the CBB asks
Every year
quiz.explanation: The policy must require all approved persons to declare their other interests in writing every year to the board or a designated committee. A one-off declaration at appointment would miss later changes.

quiz.question: Which set of committees must the board of a Bahraini bank establish under HC-3.3.1?
options: Audit, risk, remuneration and nomination
Audit, credit, IT and marketing
Risk, procurement, HR and treasury
Audit, strategy, branding and IT
quiz.explanation: HC-3.3.1 requires audit, risk, remuneration and nomination committees. A corporate governance committee is recommended as Guidance; the other committees listed are not required by Module HC.

quiz.question: A teller reports through the whistleblowing channel that her manager overrides limits. The manager finds out and moves her to night shifts. Which Module HC duty is most directly at stake?
options: Protecting staff who raise concerns from reprisal
Rotating internal audit staff periodically
Holding four board meetings a year
Disclosing directors' attendance at the AGM
quiz.explanation: HC-1.2.3(b) makes the board responsible for protecting staff who raise concerns from detrimental treatment or reprisal. Moving her to night shifts is the kind of reprisal the board must prevent.

quiz.question: Can a Bahraini bank's whistleblowing arrangements cover escalating material concerns to the CBB?
options: No, concerns must stay inside the bank and go only to the audit committee
Yes, Module HC includes escalating material concerns to the CBB
Only after the external auditor agrees
Only for concerns raised by customers
quiz.explanation: HC-1.2.2 says the whistleblowing policy and procedures include escalation of material concerns to the CBB. Keeping every concern inside the bank or requiring the auditor's consent would contradict it.

quiz.question: Arad Bay's CEO asks to join the risk committee 'to keep it practical'. What does Module HC say?
options: He may join as a non-voting chair
He may join once the CBB is notified
The CEO and senior management must not be members
He may join if the committee has at least five independent members
quiz.explanation: HC-3.5.3 says the CEO and other senior management must not be members of the risk committee. Management can report to the committee, but membership would undermine its independent oversight.

quiz.question: Every five years the audit committee commissions a quality review of internal audit and compliance. Who must carry it out?
options: The bank's own external auditor
The head of internal audit himself
A team drawn from the compliance function
A third-party consultant other than the external auditor
quiz.explanation: HC-3.4.6(m) requires a third-party consultant other than the external auditor, with results provided to the CBB. Self-review by internal audit or compliance would not be independent.

quiz.question: Arad Bay wants to merge its remuneration and nomination committees. What does Module HC require?
options: A board resolution and nothing more
Shareholder approval at the AGM, without any need to involve the CBB
No conflict between their duties and the CBB's prior approval
Notice to the CBB after the merger
quiz.explanation: HC-3.3.3 allows committees to be combined only if no conflict of interest arises between their duties and subject to the CBB's prior approval. Notice after the event or a board resolution alone is not enough.

quiz.question: Arad Bay's audit committee has three members: two independent directors and the CFO. What is wrong under Module HC?
options: Senior managers such as the CFO must not sit on the audit committee
Nothing, since two of the three members are independent directors
The committee needs at least five members
The CFO must chair the committee instead
quiz.explanation: HC-3.4.3 says the CEO and other senior management must not be members of the audit committee. A majority of independents does not cure having an executive member.

sessions.title: Director Selection, Induction and Ongoing Training (Module HC-2 and Module FP)
sessions.summary: Who may sit on a Bahraini bank's board, how to build the formal, tailored induction HC-2.3.4 requires, and how directors keep learning through ongoing training and CPD under Modules HC and FP.
objectives: Apply Module HC's selection criteria, directorship limits and re-election rules for board candidates
Design a formal, tailored director induction that meets HC-2.3.4
Explain the continuing education duties of all directors under HC-2.3.6 and Module FP
Identify the evidence a bank keeps to show its directors are inducted, trained and competent

lines.text: Morning! I ran risk at an insurer in Stockholm and I've sat on two boards, but never on a Bahraini bank's board.
Which is exactly why you get a formal, tailored induction, not a pile of policies.
Module HC lists what it should include: meetings with senior management, site visits, strategy and financial briefings, risk and compliance, and time with the auditors and legal counsel.
And after the induction? Do I learn the rest on the job?
Not alone. Every director must keep educating themselves on the bank and its governance, and Module FP asks the bank to run ongoing training and CPD for directors.
I've booked you with internal audit on Thursday. Bring hard questions!

scenes.heading: Budget first
scenes.narration: Every year the board sets aside enough time, budget and other resources for directors' induction programmes, whether or not new directors are expected.

scenes.heading: Meet the people
scenes.narration: The new director meets senior management, the internal and external auditors and legal counsel, and hears their views first-hand.

scenes.heading: See the bank
scenes.narration: Visits to the bank's facilities show how branches, operations and technology really work.

scenes.heading: Understand the issues
scenes.narration: Presentations cover strategic plans, significant financial, accounting and risk management issues, and the compliance programmes.

scenes.heading: Keep learning
scenes.narration: Induction leads into ongoing training, using internal or external resources, so the director contributes effectively from the start of the term.

items.label: Nominate
items.detail: The nomination committee assesses skills, time and independence; the board, not management, nominates.

items.label: CBB approval
items.detail: Prior written CBB approval for the nominee under Article 65 and Module FP.

items.label: Appointment letter
items.detail: Written agreement: powers, duties, term, time commitment, committees, pay and access to independent advice.

items.label: Induction
items.detail: A formal programme tailored to the director, from the start of the term.

items.label: Ongoing training
items.detail: Training and CPD tailored to the person, with regular regulatory updates.

items.label: Annual evaluation
items.detail: Board, committee and individual reviews feed training needs and re-election.

cards.question: Which of these does Module HC specifically list as part of a new director's induction?
options: A written examination set by the CBB before the first board meeting
Meetings with the internal and external auditors and legal counsel
Six months shadowing a long-serving director before voting
A banking qualification completed within the first year
cards.explanation: HC-2.3.4(c) lists meetings with senior management, site visits, presentations on strategy, financial, accounting and risk issues and compliance programmes, and meetings with internal and external auditors and legal counsel. It does not prescribe exams, shadowing periods or qualifications.

cards.title: Who can sit on the board (HC-2.2 and FP-1.3.9)
cards.body:
Module HC says board candidates must have:

- the **knowledge, skills, experience** and, for non-executives, **independence of mind** for the bank's business and risk profile;
- a **record of integrity and good repute**;
- **enough time** for the role; and
- **no conflicts** that expose them to undue influence.

**Limits:** no more than **three directorships of public companies in Bahrain**, and no more than **two directorships of Bahraini banks**, never two in the same licence category. A CEO who resigned, retired or was terminated may not sit on the same bank's board. Each election proposal sets a term of **no more than three years**.

Module FP's consultation text adds that directors need enough knowledge and experience to challenge senior management, a good grasp of the industry and regulation, governance and oversight experience, and time for the role.

cards.title: Re-election done right
cards.prompt: Put Arad Bay's steps for proposing a director's re-election in a sensible order.
steps: The board evaluates each director's work, attendance and contribution
The nomination committee reviews the results and the director's other commitments
The chair confirms that the director remains effective and committed
The board prepares its recommendation with biography, other directorships, relationships and a term of up to three years
Shareholders vote at the general meeting, with the director's attendance percentage reported

cards.title: Numbers every director should know
cards.caption: From the CBB-hosted text of the revised Module HC.

items.label: Public company boards
items.detail: Maximum directorships in Bahraini public companies (HC-2.2.2).

items.label: Bahraini bank boards
items.detail: Maximum, and never two in the same licence category.

items.label: Longest term
items.detail: Per election or re-election proposal (HC-2.2.5).

items.label: Independence lost
items.detail: After three consecutive terms as an independent director.

items.label: Attendance
items.detail: Minimum share of board meetings each director attends a year.

cards.title: Marcus asks for a plan
cards.setting: Café near Bahrain Bay, a month later.

lines.text: The induction was excellent. But I come from insurance. I'm weak on bank capital rules and Bahrain's AML law.
Then your training plan is built around you. Module FP's consultation text says directors' training should be customised, with the board's collective knowledge in mind.
Is there a minimum number of hours for directors?

For directors that text asks for induction, ongoing training and CPD on the business, the industry and compliance duties, without fixing hours. The 15-hour minimum applies to people heading senior management functions.
And continuing directors are invited to orientation sessions too. Nobody on this board is finished learning.

cards.title: The director who skips training
cards.situation: A long-serving director tells Huda he will not attend this year's board session on new CBB rules: 'I have sat on boards for twenty years. I know governance.' His board evaluation shows he rarely contributes on risk or compliance items.

choices.text: Raise it with the chair, record the gap in his evaluation, agree a tailored plan with him and let the nomination committee weigh it at re-election
choices.outcome: Best answer. HC-2.3.6 expects all directors to keep educating themselves, and the board's evaluation process exists to act on gaps like this one. A tailored plan respects his experience while closing the gap.

choices.text: Accept his refusal and note it in the minutes
choices.outcome: Recording it is honest, but it leaves a known gap unaddressed. Supervisors would ask what the board did about it.

choices.text: Exempt him, since experienced directors are outside the training duties
choices.outcome: There is no experience exemption. Module HC says all directors must continually educate themselves on the bank's business and governance.

choices.text: Email him the slides and record him as trained
choices.outcome: That creates a false training record. If the CBB tests the evidence, the bank's whole file loses credibility.

cards.title: Induction content and its purpose
cards.prompt: Match each part of the HC-2.3.4 induction to what it gives a new director.

pairs.right: Know who runs what and how information reaches the board
See operations, branches and technology first-hand
Grasp the plan, the numbers and the significant accounting issues
Learn the risk profile, appetite and compliance programmes
Hear independent views on controls, findings and legal exposure

cards.question: Under the CBB-hosted consultation text of Module FP, how should a director's training plan be set?
options: Identical for every director, to keep things fair
Set each year by the CBB for every bank
Customised to the director, keeping the board's collective knowledge in view
Left to each director to arrange privately
cards.explanation: FP-1.4.2 in the consultation text says board training needs and plans should be customised to individual directors, with the board's collective knowledge in mind. A single identical course ignores individual gaps, and the CBB does not set each bank's plan.

cards.title: Real case: the CBB's fit and proper webinar (April 2025)
cards.body:
On **20 April 2025** the CBB reported that it had organised a webinar introducing its new requirements for appointing board members and senior management, following the issue of the Fit and Proper Module.

- The CBB's Acting Executive Director of Banking Supervision linked the rules to the Financial Services Sector Development Strategy 2022-2026 and said they make **chief executives directly responsible** for the suitability of people in senior management positions.
- The Director of Regulatory Policy explained how the rules work in practice and the criteria for assessing candidates, describing a shift towards licensees taking a **more proactive role**.
- Chief executives and compliance officers of licensees attended.

**Lesson for Arad Bay:** when the rules change, the regulator briefs the industry. The bank's job is to cascade that learning to its board and senior managers, and to record that it did.

Source: CBB press release, 20 April 2025, cbb.gov.bh.

cards.title: Make induction and training evidence-ready
cards.body:
- Keep an **induction checklist** signed by the director and the company secretary.
- Record dates, presenters, materials and attendance for every session.
- Link each training item to a gap found in the **board evaluation**.
- Report the induction and training budget used against the amount allocated.
- Module FP's consultation text lists training material, attendance and evaluation among the records to keep for **at least five years** after a person leaves.

cards.title: Stage 3 take-aways
items: Candidates need skills, integrity, time and freedom from conflicts; limits apply to public company and Bahraini bank directorships.
The board funds induction every year; each new director gets a formal, tailored induction with access to ongoing training.
Induction includes senior management, site visits, strategy, financial, risk and compliance briefings, auditors and counsel.
All directors must keep educating themselves; Module FP asks banks for director induction, ongoing training and CPD.
The fixed 15-hour CPD minimum in the FP consultation text is for heads of senior management functions, not directors.

cards.prompt: If you joined a bank board tomorrow, which three topics would you most need in your induction, and who in the bank should brief you on each?

quiz.question: Who must allocate time, budget and other resources every year for directors' induction programmes?
options: The CBB
The external auditor
The board
Each director personally
quiz.explanation: HC-2.3.4(a) places this on the board: sufficient time, budget and resources must be allocated annually. The CBB does not fund banks' inductions and directors are not expected to pay for their own.

quiz.question: Under HC-2.3.6, which directors must continually educate themselves about the bank's business and governance?
options: Only new directors in their first year
Only the independent directors
Only audit committee members
All directors
quiz.explanation: HC-2.3.6 says all directors must continually educate themselves on the bank's business and corporate governance, and continuing directors are invited to orientation meetings. There is no exemption by seniority or role.

quiz.question: A candidate sits on the boards of one Bahraini retail bank and one Bahraini wholesale bank. Arad Bay wants to nominate her. What does Module HC say?
options: She can if she resigns one seat within a year
She cannot take a third Bahraini bank board seat
She can if the CBB is told afterwards
She can, as the limit covers public companies only
quiz.explanation: HC-2.2.2(f) limits a director to two directorships of Bahraini banks. Joining Arad Bay would make three. The separate public company limit does not replace the bank limit.

quiz.question: A candidate sits on the board of one Bahraini retail bank. Arad Bay is also a retail bank. Can she join Arad Bay's board?
options: No, two seats in the same licence category are not allowed
Yes, as the limit is two Bahraini bank boards
Yes, if she is classed as an independent director on both bank boards
Yes, if both banks' chairs agree in writing
quiz.explanation: Module HC caps Bahraini bank directorships at two and adds that two directorships within the same licence category, such as two retail banks, are not permitted.

quiz.question: Arad Bay's former CEO has just retired. Can he join Arad Bay's board?
options: Yes, once a one-year cooling-off period has passed since he retired
Yes, but only as a non-executive director
No, a former CEO may not sit on the same bank's board
Yes, if the CBB approves him as chair
quiz.explanation: HC-2.2.4 says a CEO who has resigned, retired or been terminated must not be appointed or retained as a board member of the same bank. Module HC gives no cooling-off route.

quiz.question: What is the longest term a director may be proposed for in a single election or re-election under HC-2.2.5?
options: Two years
Three years
Four years
Five years
quiz.explanation: Each proposal must state the term, which may not exceed three years. Longer terms would reduce shareholders' chance to review the director.

quiz.question: Marcus comes from insurance and knows little of Bahrain's AML law. What does Module FP's consultation text suggest for his training?
options: The same generic governance course that every other director attends
No training, since he has CBB approval
An AML diploma before he may vote
A plan tailored to him, with the board's collective knowledge in mind
quiz.explanation: FP-1.4.2 in the consultation text says board training needs and plans should be customised to individual directors in light of the board's collective knowledge. CBB approval does not end the need to learn.

quiz.question: What must a Bahraini bank have with each director under HC-2.3.3?
options: A written appointment agreement covering duties, term, time and pay
A personal guarantee covering the bank's liabilities during the director's term
An employment contract with a probation period
A confidentiality bond lodged with the CBB
quiz.explanation: HC-2.3.3 requires a written appointment agreement setting out powers, duties, accountability, term, time commitment, committees, remuneration, expenses and access to independent advice. Directors are not employees on probation.

quiz.question: A board evaluation shows a director rarely contributes on risk topics and missed training. What is the best use of this finding?
options: Keep it confidential until the CBB asks
Feed it into his training plan and the nomination committee's review
Remove him from the board at once, without waiting for a shareholder vote
Delete it so the governance report looks clean
quiz.explanation: Board evaluations under HC-3.1 exist to drive improvement: training for gaps and nomination committee input on re-election. Hiding or deleting findings defeats their purpose, and removal is not the first step.

quiz.question: Under FP-1.4.1 of the consultation text, what must a licensee establish for its board directors?
options: Induction, ongoing training and CPD arrangements
A fixed 40-hour CPD quota each year
An annual examination run by the CBB
Mentoring by the external auditor
quiz.explanation: FP-1.4.1 requires induction, ongoing training and CPD arrangements to educate directors on the business, the industry and compliance duties. It does not fix hours for directors.

sessions.title: Fit and Proper and Approved Persons: CBB Law Article 65 and Module FP
sessions.summary: How Article 65 of the CBB Law and Module FP decide who may serve as a director or senior manager: the three criteria, due diligence, prior CBB approval, notifications, interim arrangements and the CBB's powers.
objectives: Explain the CBB Law Article 65 approval powers and how Module FP implements them
Apply the three fit and proper criteria and the due diligence steps before an appointment
Identify which positions in a Bahraini bank need prior CBB approval and which need notification
Describe the ongoing duties: annual reassessment, notifications, interim arrangements, records and CBB action

lines.text: Our CRO is retiring. I've found a strong candidate from a bank in Kuwait. Can she start next month?
Head of risk management needs the CBB's prior written approval at a Bahraini bank. We do our own due diligence first, then apply on Form 3.
Due diligence? Her references are excellent.
We still test her honesty and integrity, financial soundness and competence against our standards, and we must take references from her previous bank.
And under Module FP, you and the board answer for her suitability. The CBB no longer co-manages most senior appointments.
So the CBB approves fewer people but we carry more responsibility. Show me the whole gate.

scenes.heading: The legal root
scenes.narration: Article 65 of the CBB Law requires prior CBB approval for board nominees and executive posts and lets the CBB set standards of qualification, experience and training.

scenes.heading: Principles
scenes.narration: Licensees keep unsuitable people off the board and out of senior roles, assess them before appointment and keep checking suitability afterwards.

scenes.heading: Own standards
scenes.narration: Each bank adopts board-approved recruitment, training and competency policies. The CBB's appendix of qualifications is illustrative, not a minimum.

scenes.heading: Approval gate
scenes.narration: Directors and a short list of key senior roles still need the CBB's written approval before they take up the post.

scenes.heading: Tell the CBB
scenes.narration: Banks report suitability concerns, departures and other changes quickly, and keep records that prove how they made their decisions.

cards.title: Approval or notification? (Bahraini bank)
cards.caption: From the CBB-hosted consultation text of Module FP (October 2024). Check the final Common Volume text for the current list and deadlines.

items.label: Board
items.right: Resignation, suspension, dismissal or disciplinary action: within one working day

items.label: Top executives
items.right: Other senior management appointments: name, position and contact details

items.label: Finance and control
items.left: Heads of finance, risk management and compliance
items.right: Information that someone no longer meets fit and proper: immediately

items.label: Financial crime
items.right: Transfers to another role or group entity: within one working day

cards.question: Which Arad Bay appointment needs the CBB's prior written approval under Appendix FP-2 of the consultation text for Bahraini banks?
options: Head of retail branches
Head of marketing
Head of human resources
Head of compliance
cards.explanation: For Bahraini banks the consultation list covers the CEO and deputy CEO, head of finance, head of risk management, head of compliance and the MLRO, plus all board directors. Other senior management functions are notified to the CBB rather than approved in advance.

cards.title: The three fit and proper criteria (FP-1.3)
cards.body:
A bank's fit and proper criteria must cover three areas (consultation text):

**1. Honesty, integrity and reputation.** A person fails if, for example, convicted of a crime involving honesty (unless restored to good standing), disqualified as a director, or refused or restricted a licence. The bank also weighs wider conduct: dismissals, disciplinary records, regulatory censures and any lack of openness with regulators.

**2. Financial soundness.** Relevant factors include bankruptcy in the last five years, an unpaid court judgment debt and serious or persistent failure to manage debts that caused loss to others.

**3. Competency.** Qualifications, relevant experience and the ability to manage, measured against the bank's own standards. For senior managers that includes markets, risk, governance, financial reporting and regulation.

Suitability is assessed **before appointment** and again in an **annual** assessment.

cards.title: Which criterion is at stake?
cards.prompt: Sort each finding from Arad Bay's due diligence into the fit and proper criterion it tests.

items.text: Disqualified as a company director in another country
Dismissed by a former employer for falsifying reports
Was not open with a regulator during an inspection
An unpaid court judgment from a business deal
Declared bankrupt three years ago
Persistent failure to manage debts, causing losses to others
Candidate for head of risk has never worked in risk management
Candidate lacks knowledge of Bahrain's regulatory framework

items.label: Set standards
items.detail: Board-approved competency standards for the role.

items.label: Due diligence
items.detail: Background, qualifications and references from previous financial institutions, all documented.

items.label: Apply on Form 3
items.detail: Only for candidates who meet the criteria; written approval before appointment.

items.label: CBB review
items.detail: The CBB may look into past conduct, weighing seriousness, relevance and time elapsed.

items.label: Sign the SOR
items.detail: Statement of responsibilities signed within one month of appointment (consultation text).

items.label: Reassess yearly
items.detail: Ongoing suitability assessed every year and recorded.

lines.text: A court case has been filed against our new head of finance over a commercial dispute at his previous company. He told us yesterday.
It's only filed. Nothing is proven. Do we have to say anything?
Yes. Module FP says we notify the CBB immediately when we learn of information suggesting someone may no longer meet fit and proper requirements, and it gives legal cases as an example.
Then we also assess it ourselves: how serious it is, how relevant to his role, and what he told us when we hired him.
And our assessment goes on his file. If we can't show our reasoning, the CBB will assume we never did it.

cards.title: Filling a vacancy
cards.situation: Arad Bay's head of compliance resigns with two weeks' notice. The CEO wants the deputy head, who has never been assessed against the bank's fit and proper criteria, to act as head 'until we find someone, however long it takes'.

choices.text: Notify the CBB of the resignation within one working day, assess the deputy before the interim appointment, and plan a CBB-approved permanent appointment within 120 days
choices.outcome: Best answer. The consultation text requires prompt notice, interim cover by someone who meets the criteria and a permanent appointment within 120 days, and the head of compliance needs prior CBB approval.

choices.text: Notify the CBB and start recruiting, but decide on interim cover later
choices.outcome: Notice and recruitment are right, but the role cannot be left uncovered. Interim arrangements must keep the duties running, using someone who meets the criteria.

choices.text: Let the deputy act for as long as needed; interim roles need no checks
choices.outcome: Internal interim appointees must meet the fit and proper criteria, and the vacancy has to be filled permanently within the set period.

choices.text: Appoint the deputy permanently today and seek CBB approval afterwards
choices.outcome: The head of compliance of a Bahraini bank needs the CBB's prior written approval. Appointing first and asking later breaks the approval rule.

cards.front: Myth: the CBB's appendix sets minimum qualifications.
cards.back: Fact: the qualifications in Appendix FP-1 are illustrative. Each bank sets its own competency standards.

cards.front: Myth: fit and proper is checked only at hiring.
cards.back: Fact: suitability is reassessed every year, and material deficiencies are reported to the CBB promptly.

cards.front: Myth: fewer CBB approvals means less accountability.
cards.back: Fact: the board and CEO now answer for the suitability of senior managers the CBB no longer approves.

cards.front: Myth: an approved person can be moved to any role.
cards.back: Fact: moving to another position that needs approval requires the CBB's approval for that move.

cards.front: Myth: references are optional for strong candidates.
cards.back: Fact: reference checks are required when hiring from another financial institution, in Bahrain or abroad.

cards.front: Myth: a CBB approval can never be undone.
cards.back: Fact: in the consultation text, the CBB may treat an approval as revoked if it learns the person never met the criteria.

cards.question: Article 65 of the CBB Law allows the CBB to do which of the following?
options: Require a licensee to stop an unsuitable official acting as a director or executive
Appoint a bank's directors directly, without a shareholder vote
Set the salaries of every bank executive in Bahrain
Approve every new employee a bank hires
cards.explanation: Article 65 requires prior approval for board nominees and executive posts, lets the CBB set qualification, experience and training standards, and lets it require a licensee to stop an unqualified or unsuitable official from performing a board or executive role. It does not make the CBB the employer or pay-setter.

cards.title: Real case: the CBB's new fit and proper rules (March 2025)
cards.body:
On **4 March 2025** the CBB announced new rules on appointing board members and senior management:

- One **common module** for all licensees replaced the fit and proper parts of the Licensing Requirements, Authorisation and Training and Competency modules across the Rulebook volumes.
- **Fewer senior managers** need CBB prior approval, and the prescriptive 'one size fits all' qualifications were removed; licensees now set their own standards.
- The CBB said it would no longer co-manage senior appointments, making the **board and CEO accountable** for the suitability of senior managers.
- Prior-approval rules applied from **1 April 2025**, the rest from **1 October 2025**.

**Lesson:** less pre-approval means more self-assessment. A bank must be able to show its own standards, checks and reasoning.

Source: CBB press release, 4 March 2025, cbb.gov.bh.

cards.title: Real case: approved person notices in capital markets (2023-2024)
cards.body:
The CBB's Capital Markets Supervision Directorate publishes a **Compliance and Enforcement Annual Report**. The 2024 edition lists non-compliance letters sent to self-regulatory organisations, such as exchanges:

- **2023:** two letters for **failing to notify the CBB of an approved person's resignation**.
- **2024:** one letter for **delay in appointing a head of risk management**.

The report explains that material cases can go to the CBB's **Enforcement Decision Review Committee**, and its orders can be appealed to the CBB's Appeals Committee within 30 days.

**Lesson for Arad Bay:** these were market institutions, not banks, but the duties are the same in kind. Missed notices and long vacancies in control roles are visible, countable failures.

Source: CBB CMSD Compliance and Enforcement Annual Report 2024, cbb.gov.bh.

cards.title: Stage 4 take-aways
items: Article 65 of the CBB Law requires prior approval for board nominees and executives and lets the CBB set standards and remove unsuitable officials.
Module FP's criteria cover honesty, integrity and reputation; financial soundness; and competency against the bank's own standards.
Due diligence, documented reference checks and annual reassessment are the bank's job, before and after any CBB approval.
At a Bahraini bank, directors, the CEO and deputy CEO, heads of finance, risk and compliance, and the MLRO need prior approval.
Notify suitability concerns immediately and departures quickly; keep interim cover fit and proper and fill vacancies on time.

cards.prompt: If a regulator asked you tomorrow to prove that your manager is fit and proper, what evidence exists, and what would be missing?

quiz.question: Under Article 65 of the CBB Law, what must a licensee obtain before appointing a board nominee?
options: Approval from the Ministry of Interior
A certificate of good conduct only
Approval from its external auditor
The CBB's prior approval
quiz.explanation: Article 65(a) requires prior CBB approval for nominees to the board and for executive posts. A good conduct certificate may support due diligence but does not replace CBB approval.

quiz.question: Which three areas must a licensee's fit and proper criteria cover under FP-1.3.1?
options: Age, nationality and place of residence
Honesty and integrity; financial soundness; competency
Education, salary history and references
Shareholding, seniority and length of tenure
quiz.explanation: FP-1.3.1 lists honesty, integrity and reputation; financial soundness; and competency. References are part of due diligence, not a criterion in their own right.

quiz.question: Arad Bay wants to appoint a new head of risk management. In what order must it act?
options: Complete its own due diligence, then apply for CBB approval
Appoint her first, then notify the CBB within one month of her start date
Ask the CBB to do the due diligence for it
Apply on Form 3, then check her if approved
quiz.explanation: FP-2.1.2 says licensees perform their own due diligence before seeking approval and apply only for people who meet the criteria. The CBB's review does not replace the bank's checks.

quiz.question: Arad Bay appoints a new head of treasury, a senior management function that is not on Appendix FP-2. What does the consultation text require?
options: Seek the CBB's prior written approval on Form 3 before the person starts
Nothing, since only listed roles concern the CBB
Notify the CBB of the name, position and contact details
Publish the appointment in the Official Gazette
quiz.explanation: FP-3.1.2 requires notification of appointments to senior management functions that are not CBB-approved, with name, position and contact details. Prior approval applies only to the Appendix FP-2 list.

quiz.question: Under the consultation text, when must a person in a senior management function sign their statement of responsibilities?
options: Within one week of appointment
Within six months of appointment
Within one month of appointment
Before the next general meeting
quiz.explanation: FP-1.2.3 requires a statement of responsibilities for each senior management function, signed by the person within one month of appointment.

quiz.question: Arad Bay's head of finance resigns. Under the consultation text, how quickly must the bank notify the CBB?
options: Within one working day
Within five working days
Within 30 calendar days
At the next prudential meeting
quiz.explanation: FP-3.1.3 requires notice within one working day when a director or senior management function holder resigns, is suspended, dismissed, transferred or disciplined.

quiz.question: A senior management function falls vacant. Under the consultation text, by when must a permanent appointment be made?
options: Within 30 days of the vacancy
Within 120 days of the vacancy
Within 60 days of the vacancy
Within 12 months of the vacancy
quiz.explanation: FP-3.2.1 requires interim arrangements that keep the duties running and a permanent appointment within 120 days of the vacancy.

quiz.question: Arad Bay hires a manager who previously worked at a bank in Dubai. What does FP-1.3.11 require?
options: A CBB interview before the start date
A guarantee from the previous employer
Nothing, because employers outside Bahrain fall outside the requirement
Documented reference checks with the previous institution
quiz.explanation: FP-1.3.11 requires reference checks whenever a licensee employs someone who previously worked at another financial institution, in Bahrain or elsewhere, with adequate documentation.

quiz.question: After approving a person, the CBB learns he never met the fit and proper criteria. What may it do under the consultation text?
options: Nothing, because approvals are final
Fine the person's former employer
Transfer the person to another bank
Treat the approval as revoked and agree corrective action
quiz.explanation: FP-2.1.4 lets the CBB consider the approval revoked and agree a corrective plan with the licensee; the bank or nominee may appeal within 30 calendar days.

quiz.question: Which statement about the qualifications in Appendix FP-1 reflects Module FP?
options: They are the minimum for every bank
They are illustrative; each bank sets its own standards
They apply only to foreign bank branches
They replace the bank's own competency policy and must be adopted as written
quiz.explanation: FP-1.1.3 says the appendix gives illustrative qualifications and core competencies and is not a minimum requirement. Banks must set their own board-approved standards.

sessions.title: Senior Management, Control Functions and Training Plans: Ready for the CBB
sessions.summary: Training and competence duties for senior management, risk, compliance and internal audit, the compliance officer's awareness sessions for all staff, the records the CBB expects and the enforcement tools behind them.
objectives: Explain the competence and training duties of senior management (HC-6.1.2) and heads of senior management functions (FP-1.4.3)
Describe the training duties for risk, compliance and internal audit staff under HC-7, HC-8 and HC-9
Explain the compliance officer's written guidance and awareness sessions for all staff
Assemble the records and reports the CBB expects and recall its enforcement tools

cards.title: Six days to the prudential meeting

lines.text: The supervisors will ask how we keep people competent, from this board down to our compliance analysts.
Do I personally need a training plan? I've been a banker for twenty-five years.
Yes. You head a senior management function. Module FP's consultation text asks for a yearly needs assessment, an annual plan and at least 15 hours of CPD a year.
Module HC also makes me arrange ongoing training for my auditors, and risk staff must be trained regularly too.
And my team runs compliance awareness sessions for all staff, sponsored by you, Salman. That's in HC-8.
Then let's pull it together. One stage left before we face the board.

scenes.heading: Senior management
scenes.narration: Senior managers are chosen for their competence and receive regular training to keep their skills current in their areas of responsibility.

scenes.heading: Annual plan
scenes.narration: For heads of senior management functions, the bank assesses training needs every year and keeps an annual plan with methods, deadlines, review and CPD.

scenes.heading: Risk function
scenes.narration: Risk staff need market, product and risk knowledge and regular training. The CRO also reminds all staff of risk requirements, with the CEO's sponsorship.

scenes.heading: Compliance
scenes.narration: Compliance staff get regular, systematic training on new laws and standards. The compliance officer issues written guidance and runs awareness sessions for staff.

scenes.heading: Internal audit
scenes.narration: The head of internal audit arranges ongoing training so auditors keep up with new products, processes and growing technical complexity.

cards.title: Who must be trained, and where it is written
cards.caption: Module HC paragraphs from the CBB-hosted revised text; FP paragraphs from the October 2024 consultation text.

items.label: Directors
items.right: Induction, ongoing training and continuous self-education

items.label: Senior management
items.right: Regular training to maintain competence and stay current

items.label: SMF heads
items.right: Yearly needs assessment, annual plan, at least 15 CPD hours a year

items.label: Risk staff
items.right: Qualified, experienced and subject to regular training

items.label: Compliance staff
items.right: Regular, systematic training on laws, regulations and standards

items.label: Internal audit staff
items.right: Ongoing training arranged by the head of internal audit

items.label: All staff
items.right: Written compliance guidance and CEO-sponsored awareness sessions

cards.question: Under the CBB-hosted consultation text of Module FP, what is the minimum annual CPD for a person heading a senior management function?
options: 10 hours
15 hours
20 hours
30 hours
cards.explanation: FP-1.4.3(e) in the consultation text requires a CPD programme of not less than 15 hours a year within the annual training plan. Check the final Module FP in the Common Volume for the current wording.

cards.title: Inside an FP training plan (FP-1.4.3 and FP-1.4.4)
Building the annual SMF training plan
cards.prompt: Put the steps of Arad Bay's annual training cycle for heads of senior management functions in order.
steps: Assess each person's training needs against the bank's competency standards
Agree the specific needs and learning methods with each person
Set completion deadlines, including at least 15 CPD hours
Deliver the training and record attendance, materials and evaluations
Review results in the annual competence assessment and update the plan

cards.title: The compliance officer's loop (HC-8.1.7 and HC-8.1.8)

items.label: Identify risk
items.detail: Assess compliance risk in products, business changes and new regulations.

items.label: Guide staff
items.detail: Issue written guidance on applying laws and regulations correctly.

items.label: Raise awareness
items.detail: Run awareness sessions for staff on compliance policy, sponsored by the CEO.

items.label: Test
items.detail: Risk-based compliance testing, with results reported to the audit committee.

items.label: Report
items.detail: Quarterly to the audit committee; material failures immediately.

lines.text: As an audit committee member: how do we know our compliance team is actually trained, not just busy?
We keep their training log against a plan, and the committee receives the compliance programme and the testing results.
And every five years the audit committee commissions an outside quality review of internal audit and compliance, by a firm other than our external auditor.
When is the next one due?
Next year. The results go to the CBB by 30 September of that year.

cards.title: The training budget cut
cards.situation: Under cost pressure, the CFO proposes cutting the compliance and internal audit training budgets by 80% and cancelling this year's CEO-sponsored compliance awareness sessions. 'Compliance is a cost centre,' he says.

choices.text: Reject the cut: Module HC requires regular training for compliance, audit and risk staff and staff awareness sessions, and says compliance is not a cost centre; find savings elsewhere and minute the decision
