choices.outcome: Best answer. The training duties for control functions and the awareness sessions are written into Module HC, and HC-8.1.3 says compliance should not be seen as a cost centre. The board and audit committee must keep these functions resourced.

choices.text: Keep the awareness sessions but stop all specialist training for compliance and audit staff
choices.outcome: Half right. Staff awareness continues, but compliance and audit staff must still be trained regularly to keep up with new rules, products and risks.

choices.text: Approve the cut, since training is only good practice
choices.outcome: These are not optional extras: HC-8.1.9, HC-9.1.7 and HC-7.1.3 set training duties for control function staff.

choices.text: Replace all training with one annual email from compliance
choices.outcome: An email is not regular, systematic training, and it cannot show that staff understood anything. Supervisors would see through it.

cards.title: Records the CBB may ask for
cards.prompt: Match each record to what it should contain.

pairs.right: CVs, screening results, background and reference checks, qualifications
Standards, annual training plans, materials, attendance and evaluations
Hours completed by each person heading a senior management function
Reviews of the board, its committees and each director, reported to shareholders
All reports since the last prudential meeting, sent at least three weeks before it

cards.question: Which of these powers does the CBB Law give the CBB when a licensee breaches the law or its regulations?
options: Ordering the licensee's external auditor to resign
Setting the pay of the licensee's directors
Issuing a public statement on the breach
Issuing binding court judgments against staff
cards.explanation: Article 132 of the CBB Law lets the CBB publish a statement on a breach by a licensee or its officials, in proportion to the violation. The law also provides administrative fines, an observer on the board, administration and suspension of services. It does not set directors' pay or replace the courts.

cards.title: Real case: CBB enforcement and its toolkit (2023-2024)
cards.body:
The CBB's annual reports state that, under Article 38 of the CBB Law, its **Conventional Banking Supervision Directorates** took:

- **15 enforcement actions** against licensees in **2023**, including penalties; and
- **2 enforcement actions** in **2024**, including penalties.

The reports do not name the banks or the breaches, so treat these as context, not case studies.

The tools behind them are in the CBB Law: **administrative fines** (Article 129), an **observer on the board** or **administration** if restrictions fail (Article 130), **suspension** of regulated services for up to twelve months in total (Article 131) and **public censure** (Article 132). Module FP's consultation text adds individual measures: disqualification, a direction to remove or move a person, remediation such as gaining qualifications and, in extreme cases, criminal referral.

Sources: CBB Annual Reports 2023 and 2024; CBB Law, cbb.gov.bh.

cards.title: Arad Bay's readiness checklist
cards.body:
- Board and committee **charters** current; **evaluations** done and reported to shareholders.
- Director **induction** and **ongoing training** records, with budget used.
- **Annual training plans** and **CPD hours** for every head of a senior management function.
- **Training logs** for risk, compliance and internal audit staff; awareness session attendance.
- **Conflict declarations**, related-party approvals and the **whistleblowing** log.
- **FP assessments**, signed statements of responsibilities, CBB approvals and notifications.

cards.title: Stage 5 take-aways
items: Senior managers must be trained regularly (HC-6.1.2); SMF heads get a yearly needs assessment, an annual plan and 15+ CPD hours (FP consultation text).
Risk, compliance and internal audit staff must be qualified and regularly trained; the head of internal audit arranges auditors' training.
The compliance officer issues written guidance and runs CEO-sponsored awareness sessions; the CRO reminds all staff of risk requirements.
Keep training plans, materials, attendance, assessments and CPD hours for at least five years after a person leaves.
The CBB can fine, censure, suspend, appoint an observer or place a bank under administration, and act against individuals.

cards.prompt: Look at your own last twelve months of learning. Could you show a regulator a plan, the hours you completed and how the training changed your work?

quiz.question: What does HC-6.1.2 require of senior management on training?
options: Regular training to keep competencies current
One course at the start of their career
Training only when the CBB requests it
Training delegated entirely to deputies
quiz.explanation: HC-6.1.2(c) says senior management must be subject to regular training to maintain and enhance competencies and stay up to date in their areas.

quiz.question: Under the consultation text of FP-1.4.3, what minimum annual CPD applies to persons heading senior management functions?
options: 10 hours
20 hours
15 hours
40 hours
quiz.explanation: FP-1.4.3(e) requires a CPD programme of not less than 15 hours a year within the annual training plan. Check the final Common Volume text for the current wording.

quiz.question: Arad Bay's CEO says the annual training plan does not apply to him. Is he right?
options: Yes, CEOs are exempt as approved persons
Yes, if he has more than twenty years of banking experience behind him
No, but only the CBB can set his plan
No, he heads a senior management function and is covered
quiz.explanation: The CEO heads a senior management function, so FP-1.4.3's annual needs assessment, plan and CPD apply. Seniority and experience are not exemptions, and the bank, not the CBB, sets the plan.

quiz.question: Under HC-8.1.7, who runs awareness sessions for staff on compliance policy, and under whose sponsorship?
options: The head of HR, sponsored by the board chair
The compliance officer, sponsored by the CEO
The external auditor, sponsored by the CBB
The CRO, sponsored by the audit committee
quiz.explanation: HC-8.1.7(d) gives the compliance officer this task under the CEO's sponsorship, alongside written guidance to staff. The CRO has a parallel duty to remind staff of risk requirements, not compliance policy.

quiz.question: Under HC-9.1.7(e), who arranges ongoing training for internal audit staff?
options: The head of internal audit
The external auditor
The CBB's inspection team
The chief financial officer
quiz.explanation: The head of internal audit must arrange appropriate ongoing training so the team keeps up with the bank's growing technical complexity and new products and processes.

quiz.question: Arad Bay plans to staff its compliance team with untrained graduates and no development plan. Which requirement does this fail?
options: Compliance must be outsourced to specialists
Compliance staff must be qualified and regularly trained
Compliance staff must all be CBB-approved
Compliance must report to the head of finance rather than to the audit committee
quiz.explanation: HC-8.1.9 requires compliance staff to have the right qualifications and experience, understand the law and receive regular, systematic training. Module HC forbids outsourcing compliance rather than requiring it.

quiz.question: How must the compliance officer report material compliance failures to the audit committee?
options: In the next quarterly report
Only in the annual report
Only if the CEO agrees
Immediately, as they arise
quiz.explanation: HC-8.1.7(e) requires quarterly reporting on compliance risk and immediate reporting of material compliance failures, such as those risking sanctions, loss or reputation.

quiz.question: The CFO calls compliance 'a cost centre' and wants to cut its training. What does HC-8.1.3 say about that view?
options: Compliance can be cut like any cost centre
Compliance budgets are set by the CBB
Compliance should not be seen as a cost centre
Compliance training is only Guidance
quiz.explanation: HC-8.1.3(d) says the board, audit committee and management must not consider compliance a cost centre but an activity that helps avoid enforcement and protects reputation.

quiz.question: Before Arad Bay's prudential meeting, what must it send the CBB's supervisory contact about compliance?
options: A summary slide deck presented on the day of the meeting, with the minutes to follow
Only high-risk reports, after the meeting
Nothing, since the CBB collects reports on site
All compliance reports since the last meeting, at least three weeks before
quiz.explanation: HC-8.1.10 requires all compliance reports issued since the last prudential meeting, with status updates, to reach the CBB's supervisory point of contact at least three weeks before the meeting.

quiz.question: Under the FP consultation text, how long must records such as annual training plans and CPD hours be kept?
options: At least two years from the training date
Until the next CBB inspection
At least five years after employment ends
Only while the person is employed
quiz.explanation: FP-3.3.1 requires fit and proper and competence records, including training plans, attendance and CPD hours, to be kept for at least five years after the person's employment ends.

bank.question: For a branch of a foreign bank licensed by the CBB, how are references to 'the board' in Module HC read?
options: As the branch's most senior manager
As the CBB's supervisory team
As the head office or regional office
As the branch's audit committee
bank.explanation: HC-B.1.3 says that for branches of foreign banks the board means the head office or regional office. The branch must show the CBB equivalent arrangements are in place.

bank.question: Arad Bay's board meets six times this year. A director attended four meetings in person and one by video. Has he met the attendance rule?
options: Yes, five of six meets the rule and virtual attendance can count
No, only attendance in person counts
No, he needed to attend all six
Yes, because four meetings in person is the absolute minimum for any director
bank.explanation: HC-3.1.8 requires 75% attendance, in person or virtually if needed; with six meetings the table shows five. In-person-only and all-six readings are stricter than the rule.

bank.question: Where must half of a Bahraini bank's board meetings in a financial year be held?
options: At the controller's head office
Wherever the chair is based
In any GCC member state
In the Kingdom of Bahrain
bank.explanation: HC-3.1.7 requires at least four meetings a year, half of which are held in Bahrain. Other GCC states or the controller's base do not count towards that half.

bank.question: Which description of non-executive directors' role fits Module HC?
options: Running business lines alongside executives
Independent of management, scrutinising and challenging it
Approving every transaction above a limit
Representing only their nominating shareholder
bank.explanation: HC-3.1.5 requires non-executive directors to be fully independent of management and to scrutinise and challenge management constructively. Directors also represent all shareholders, not only their nominator.

bank.question: A controller nominates three of Arad Bay's nine directors. One says he must vote as the controller instructs. What does Module HC say?
options: He must vote as the controller directs
He may follow the controller's instructions on strategy but must vote freely on credit
He acts for the bank as a whole, and controllers owe a duty to minorities
He abstains on anything touching the controller
bank.explanation: HC-1.1.4 says directors consider themselves as representing all shareholders, and HC-2.1.3 says controllers' nominees must recognise their responsibility to minority shareholders. Blanket abstention is not what the module asks.

bank.question: Which statement about board minutes reflects Module HC?
options: They record key points, recommendations, decisions and any dissent
They record decisions only, to stay brief
They are optional when the board meets virtually
They leave out dissenting views so that the board always speaks with a single voice
bank.explanation: HC-3.1.6 requires minutes with key discussion points, recommendations, decisions and dissenting opinions. Dissent must be freely expressed and recorded, as HC-3.2.1 also stresses.

bank.question: Which responsibility does HC-1.1.1 give the board of a Bahraini bank?
options: Approving every new customer account
Preparing the bank's tax filings
Signing off each branch's cash count
Approving the selection of heads of risk, compliance and audit
bank.explanation: HC-1.1.1(j) makes the board, at minimum, approve the selection and oversee the performance of the CEO, CFO and heads of risk management, compliance and internal audit. The other tasks are operational.

bank.question: When must a Bahraini bank's board review the relevant parts of its governance and risk frameworks under HC-1.1.1(f)?
options: Only when the CBB orders a review
On a new activity, a material change or a major control failure
Only once every five years
Only when a director resigns
bank.explanation: HC-1.1.1(f) ties reviews to new business activities, material changes in size, strategy, markets or regulation, and major control failures. Waiting for the CBB or a fixed cycle would miss these triggers.

bank.question: Under HC-1.1.1(l), whose interests must the board consider in its decision-making?
options: The controlling shareholder only
Senior management's incentive plans only
Depositors, shareholders and other relevant stakeholders
The CBB's own budget priorities
bank.explanation: The board must consider the legitimate interests of depositors, shareholders and other relevant stakeholders. Favouring a controller alone would also conflict with duties to minority shareholders.

bank.question: A director holds 7% of the voting capital of a local company. What does Module HC require?
options: Declare it in writing in the annual declaration to the board
Nothing, as only stakes above 10% count
Sell the stake before the next board meeting or step down from the board
Report it to the CBB within one working day
bank.explanation: HC-1.2.4(g) requires approved persons to declare annually in writing their other interests, including shareholdings above 5% of a company's voting capital, to the board or a designated committee.

bank.question: Who must disclose each year which staff in controlled functions are relatives of approved persons?
options: The head of HR, to the CBB
The CEO or general manager, to the board
Each employee, to the compliance team
The audit committee, to shareholders
bank.explanation: HC-1.2.6 requires the CEO or general manager to make this disclosure to the board every year. It supports the policy's controls on employing relatives.

bank.question: An investigation confirms that a manager punished a whistleblower. What must follow under HC-1.2.3?
options: The whistleblower is moved to another department to avoid further friction
The case closes once the manager apologises
The report is deleted to protect confidentiality
The person responsible is held accountable and disciplined
bank.explanation: Once allegations are verified, HC-1.2.3(d) requires the person responsible for misconduct to be held accountable and disciplined. Moving the whistleblower would itself be detrimental treatment.

bank.question: Under HC-1.2.1(c), what message must the board send about risk-taking?
options: Risk belongs to the risk function alone, so other staff need not concern themselves
Profitable units may exceed their limits
No risk beyond appetite and limits, and every employee shares responsibility
Limits are targets to reach each year
bank.explanation: The board promotes risk awareness, does not support risk-taking beyond the appetite and limits, and makes clear all employees help keep the bank within them.

bank.question: Which requirement applies to the audit committee chair of a Bahraini bank?
options: Also the board chair, for authority
The CFO, for financial expertise
Nominated by the external auditor
Independent and not chairing any other board committee
bank.explanation: HC-3.4.2 requires the audit committee chair to be independent, not the board chair unless independent, and not the chair of any other committee. Executives such as the CFO cannot even be members.

bank.question: How often must the audit committee meet without the CEO and executive management?
options: At least once a year, with compliance, internal audit and risk present
Never, as the CEO attends every meeting
At every meeting, with the control functions also kept out of the room
Only when the CBB requests it
bank.explanation: HC-3.4.5 requires at least one meeting a year without the CEO and executives but with the compliance officer, internal auditor and risk manager, so control functions can speak freely.

bank.question: Arad Bay is assigning the role of corporate governance officer. Which statement fits Module HC?
options: It must be an external consultant
A senior manager must hold it; the compliance officer may
It must be the head of internal audit
It must be the chair of the board
bank.explanation: HC-3.8.1 requires the bank to assign the role to one of its senior management, and HC-3.8.4 allows the compliance officer to take it on. External consultants or the board chair do not meet this.

bank.question: What must the remuneration committee do about pay for approved persons and material risk-takers?
options: Leave every pay decision to the CEO
Ask the CBB to set the amounts
Set pay without regard to risk outcomes
Approve packages, considering performance and total pay
bank.explanation: HC-3.6.5(d) has the committee approve packages and amounts for each approved person and material risk-taker, based on performance evaluation and total remuneration, and review pay against risk outcomes.

bank.question: Which committee must the risk committee coordinate with to cover all risks, including emerging ones?
options: The audit committee
The marketing committee
The external auditor alone
The shareholders' meeting
bank.explanation: HC-3.5.8 requires effective communication and coordination between the audit and risk committees so that all risks, including emerging risks, are covered.

bank.question: Under HC-2.2.6, what must newly appointed non-executive directors be made aware of before nomination?
options: The bank's share price targets
Their duties, especially the time commitment
The names of major customers
Their expected annual bonus
bank.explanation: HC-2.2.6 requires new non-executive directors to be made aware of their duties before nomination, particularly the time commitment the role needs.

bank.question: Arad Bay's board set no induction budget this year because no new directors were expected. Two join mid-year. What went wrong?
options: Nothing, as budgets are needed only for expected joiners
The CBB should have funded the induction
Induction resources must be allocated every year
New directors should fund their own induction
bank.explanation: HC-2.3.4(a) requires time, budget and other resources for induction to be allocated annually, so new directors are inducted effectively from the start of their term whenever they join.

bank.question: Under HC-2.3.1, what must the chair confirm to shareholders when proposing a director's re-election?
options: The director has bought shares in the bank and attended at least half the meetings
The CBB has nominated the director
A formal evaluation shows the director is still effective and committed
The director's term will have no limit
bank.explanation: HC-2.3.1 requires the chair to confirm, after a formal performance evaluation, that the director remains effective and committed. Terms are limited to three years per proposal.

bank.question: What must accompany a board proposal to elect an independent director?
options: The director's personal bank statements
A statement that the board finds the independence criteria met
The latest CBB inspection report
A copy of the director's will
bank.explanation: HC-2.2.5(c) requires, for an independent director, a statement that the board has determined the applicable independence rules and criteria are met, alongside biography and other directorships.

bank.question: The CEO asks Arad Bay's nomination committee to recommend the next chief internal auditor. Is that right under Module HC?
options: Yes, it recommends every senior hire
Yes, the nomination committee recommends every senior hire, including the chief internal auditor
No, the CEO alone appoints the auditor
No, internal audit, risk and compliance heads come from other committees
bank.explanation: HC-3.7.3(c) excludes the chief internal auditor, CRO and chief compliance officer from the nomination committee's remit; the audit and risk committees recommend them. The CEO does not appoint them alone.

bank.question: What does FP-1.3.9 of the consultation text expect of board directors?
options: Enough experience to challenge management and a grasp of regulation
Coding skills for core banking systems
A professional actuarial qualification
Fluency in every customer language
bank.explanation: FP-1.3.9 expects sufficient knowledge and experience to challenge senior management, a good understanding of the industry and regulation, governance experience and enough time for the role.

bank.question: What may directors' training programmes include under FP-1.4.2 of the consultation text?
options: Overviews and risk profiles of new business lines, and regulatory updates
Only general management theory
Personal investment advice
Approval of marketing campaigns
bank.explanation: FP-1.4.2 suggests programmes may give directors detailed overviews and risk profiles of significant or new business lines and periodic regulatory updates, tailored to each director.

bank.question: Which statement about continuing directors fits HC-2.3.6?
options: They are excluded from orientation
They must be invited to orientation meetings
They retake full induction every year
They train only if re-elected
bank.explanation: HC-2.3.6 requires all continuing directors to be invited to orientation meetings, and all directors must keep educating themselves.

bank.question: A CEO candidate was found liable, as an officer, for a company offence caused by his neglect. What does FP-1.3.3 of the consultation text say?
options: It is irrelevant, because the offence happened outside the Kingdom of Bahrain
It matters only for financial soundness
He is treated as not meeting the honesty and integrity criterion
It counts only if the CBB discovers it
bank.explanation: FP-1.3.3(c) lists being an officer liable for a corporate offence committed with his consent, connivance or neglect as failing the honesty, integrity and reputation criterion, wherever it occurred.

bank.question: When deciding on an approval, which factors does the CBB weigh under FP-2.1.3 of the consultation text?
options: The candidate's age, nationality and salary
The bank's share price and profits
The controlling shareholder's preference
Seriousness, relevance to the role and time since the event
bank.explanation: FP-2.1.3 says the CBB considers each case's circumstances: how serious the event was, its relevance to the role and how long ago it happened.

bank.question: What must a licensee keep for each senior management function under FP-1.2.3 of the consultation text?
options: A personal guarantee from the holder
A CBB-issued licence card
A statement of responsibilities
A non-compete bond
bank.explanation: FP-1.2.3 requires a statement of responsibilities setting out the role, reporting and oversight duties, delegated authority and personal accountability, signed within one month.

bank.question: Under FP-2.1.5 of the consultation text, what must the CEO of a Bahraini bank be?
options: A Bahraini national with a banking degree
Resident in Bahrain and working full-time for the bank
A shareholder of the bank
A member of the audit committee
bank.explanation: Senior management functions listed in Appendix FP-2 must be resident in Bahrain and dedicated full-time; the listed exceptions do not cover banks. Nationality and shareholding are not requirements.

bank.question: Who identifies the senior management functions covered by Module FP?
options: The CBB, bank by bank
The external auditor
Shareholders at the AGM
The board and the chief executive officer
bank.explanation: FP-1.2.1 makes the board and CEO responsible for documenting the organisation structure and identifying senior management functions, and for their compliance with fit and proper requirements.

bank.question: Arad Bay moves its CBB-approved head of compliance to be head of risk management. What is needed?
options: CBB approval for the move, since the new role also needs approval
Nothing, as she is already an approved person and stays within the same bank
Only a resolution of the board
Only a note in the annual report
bank.explanation: FP-3.1.4 says that when an approved person transfers to another position requiring approval, the CBB's approval of the transfer is required; the move is also notified under FP-3.1.3.

bank.question: Which actions may the CBB take against individuals who fail fit and proper standards under FP-3.4.2 of the consultation text?
options: Only a written warning to the licensee
Seizure of the person's private assets
Disqualification, removal, remediation or criminal referral
Tax penalties on the individual
bank.explanation: FP-3.4.2 lists disqualification, a direction to remove or move the person, remediation requirements and, in extreme cases of dishonesty with information, referral for prosecution.

bank.question: According to the CBB's March 2025 press release, from when did Module FP's prior-approval requirements apply?
options: 1 April 2025
1 January 2025
1 October 2025
1 March 2025
bank.explanation: The CBB said the new prior-approval requirements for directors and senior managers took effect on 1 April 2025, with the remaining requirements from 1 October 2025.

bank.question: What must the annual training plan for heads of senior management functions address under FP-1.4.3 of the consultation text?
options: Salary, bonus, leave and travel
Only courses the CBB has approved
Only technical IT certifications
Needs, methods, deadlines, annual review and CPD
bank.explanation: FP-1.4.3 lists specific training needs, learning methods, the period for completion, annual review and assessment, and a CPD programme of at least 15 hours a year.

bank.question: To save costs, Arad Bay's CRO is also given a lending business line. What does HC-7.1.7 say?
options: Allowed if the risk committee agrees
Not allowed: the CRO must have no business-line role
Allowed for small business lines
Allowed if the CEO supervises closely
bank.explanation: HC-7.1.7(c) says the CRO must be independent, with no managerial or financial responsibility or approval authority over business lines, and no dual hatting.

bank.question: Under HC-7.1.7(i), what must the CRO do for all staff?
options: Regularly remind them of risk requirements, with the CEO's sponsorship
Train each employee personally every month
Approve every staff appraisal
Countersign each employee's code of conduct declaration and annual risk appraisal
bank.explanation: The CRO must consistently remind all staff, through a regular process sponsored by the CEO, of the risk management requirements, so that everyone shares a common understanding.

bank.question: Management wants to launch a digital lending product before risk and compliance have assessed it. What does Module HC require?
options: Launch now and assess after six months
Launch if the product is profitable
Launch if the CEO signs a waiver
Risk and approval processes first, or the launch is delayed
bank.explanation: HC-7.1.5 requires adequate risk management and approval processes for new products; if they are not in place, the launch must be delayed, with risk function input.

bank.question: What must the risk management function have under HC-7.1.3(e)?
options: CBB licences for each risk analyst
Revenue targets linked to lending
Enough qualified, experienced staff who are regularly trained
A seat for each analyst on the board
bank.explanation: HC-7.1.3(e) requires a sufficient number of employees with the right experience and qualifications, including market, product and risk knowledge, who are subject to regular training.

bank.question: Under HC-9.1.12, what must internal auditors appointed from within the bank not do?
options: Report findings to the audit committee
Audit work they were responsible for until a one-year cooling-off
Access the bank's records
Apply due professional care
bank.explanation: HC-9.1.12(b) bars internal auditors appointed from inside the bank from auditing activities they previously handled until a one-year cooling-off period has passed.

bank.question: Under the CBB Law, if administrative restrictions on a licensee prove futile, what may the CBB do?
options: Appoint a board observer or place the licensee under administration
Transfer its shares to the government
Dissolve the board and pick new shareholders
Close every branch of the licensee for a month without notice to customers or staff
bank.explanation: Article 130 of the CBB Law allows the CBB to appoint an observer member on the board for a set period or to place the licensee under administration when restrictions prove futile.

bank.question: What did the CBB's 2024 Annual Report say about enforcement by its conventional banking supervision directorates?
options: Fifteen enforcement actions in 2024
No enforcement actions at all in 2024
Fifty enforcement actions in 2024
Two enforcement actions in 2024, including penalties
bank.explanation: The 2024 Annual Report records two enforcement actions, including penalties. Fifteen was the 2023 figure, so the counts should not be confused.

bank.question: Under HC-8.1.2, which two functions must be kept separate?
options: Finance and treasury
Compliance and internal audit
Risk and information technology
Marketing and operations
bank.explanation: HC-8.1.2 requires the compliance function and the internal audit function to be separate, so that audit can independently review compliance's work.
